summaries.title: Is Long-Term Stock Market Momentum Slowing In A Concerning Manner?
summaries.reason: The video concludes the secular bull market remains intact: monthly and quarterly RSI are in strong (70+) territory, breadth is broadening constructively, credit (BKLN) is confirming new highs, and the model trend score is back to double 100.
summaries.summary:
• Momentum check: monthly Nasdaq RSI closed at a strong 70.11 on Aug 7 — far above the 2000–2013 secular-stagnation readings; no concerning slowdown.
• Quarterly S&P 500 RSI above 70, resembling prior secular bulls (1982–2000), with price well above an upward-sloping 10-quarter MA.
• Trend structure: S&P 500 above rising 50/150/200-day MAs; NYSE composite shows a full-board bullish MA stack.
• Breadth constructive: A/D volume line above its Bollinger centerline; mid-cap growth making new highs above a rising 200-week MA; travel/tourism index +9.5% in five sessions.
• Credit confirms: leveraged loans (BKLN) printed a new high alongside the S&P.
• Laggards (small caps, S&P 1500) look healthy in absolute terms but remain in relative downtrends — large-cap leadership persists.
• Gold: long-term holding intact, but short-term overhead resistance means patience before adding.
• Models: 136 charts / 489 binary questions read constructive; trend score back to double 100.
• Bottom line: secular bull market intact — stay patient, keep an open mind.

summaries.title: Tech/AI Trade: Healthy Pause Or Concerning Trend Reversal?
summaries.reason: The video concludes the tech/AI pullback is a healthy pause, not a reversal: the 10-year yield (the key rate) has not broken out, all major tech and large-cap-growth ratios remain in uptrends above upward-sloping AVWAP lines, and the model score as of July 31, 2026 classifies the volatility as normal - 'volatility to ignore' rather than evidence of material trend shifts.
summaries.summary:
• Question: with rates rising, is the tech/AI pullback a healthy pause or a trend reversal?
• Rates: 30-year yield broke out to a 19-year high, but ~90% of US debt is financed elsewhere and the more important 10-year (~4.745%) has NOT broken out; only a move through ~4.9% would raise concerns.
• Long-term rates are largely back to their secular trend — "relevant" does not equal "showstopper"; a real problem would show up in every chart and model score.
• Tech/AI ratios (AIQ, XLK, 1Q, MGK, IUSG vs RSP): still in uptrends above upward-sloping AVWAP lines, making higher highs; pullback only retraced to 38.2–61.8%.
• Rotation narratives fail the evidence: utilities, healthcare, industrials, energy, materials, value, dividend, small caps, Dow, and foreign all in long-term downtrends vs large-cap growth; recent RSP/small-cap/Dow new highs are countertrend moves within those downtrends.
• Model score (July 31, 2026): classifies the volatility as normal — "volatility to ignore."
• Conclusion: healthy pause, not a reversal.

summaries.title: Summer Doldrums Or Something Much Worse?
summaries.reason: The video finds no evidence of a trend change: every key index and sector ratio is still above its anchored VWAP support and normal retracement levels, model scores remain supportive, and historical drawdowns in secular bulls were always followed by higher highs. Any pullback is framed as a normal correction within an ongoing uptrend, not the start of something worse.
summaries.summary:
• Question: summer doldrums or something worse? Warning against action bias when markets are unsettled.
• Pullbacks are normal in secular bulls: S&P 500 still above the 38.2/50/61.8% retracements of the October 2022 advance and key anchored VWAP lines — no trend change.
• Semis: SMH retraced 38.2% of its move since April 2026; took 30% of profits to diversify, long-term uptrend intact.
• Nasdaq closed below one AVWAP line — more near-term pain possible, but it could retrace much further without damaging the uptrend.
• History: 16 drawdowns >6% in prior secular bulls (avg ~12%) — every one was followed by a higher high.
• Credit: bullish breakout, not a 2022-style breakdown; no defensive rotation into staples/treasuries as in 2000/2007; energy vs tech shows no inflation panic.
• Breadth: NYSE Composite near all-time highs.
• 400-ETF screen: tech/AI still top (9/9 criteria); bonds and defensives score near zero.
• Conclusion: no trend-change evidence; any pullback most likely a normal correction with higher highs to follow, possibly by Q4 2026 or into 2027.

summaries.title: Stocks: Volatility To Ignore Or Volatility To Respect?
summaries.reason: The explicit verdict is 'volatility to ignore': breadth, trend structure, and credit remain constructive and risk-on with no peaking patterns, even though short-term semis weakness justified trimming 20% of the SMH position as risk management, not a trend call.
summaries.summary:
• Verdict: "volatility to ignore" — not a prediction, but nothing alarming across 489 questions on 136 charts.
• Breadth: NYSE A/D line making higher highs, no Q4 2021/Jan 2022 divergence, nothing like 1998 or 2007 peaking; NYSE composite above a rising 200-day MA near all-time highs.
• S&P 500: rally off late March 2026 holds above 38.2/50/61.8% retracements and a rising 200-day MA, with numerous reference points below.
• Rotation: no evidence of shift away from tech — RSP/SPY, IWM/XLK, and 9 sector ETFs vs XLK all batting 0 for 5, several at all-time lows vs tech. Energy (XLE vs XLK) checked its first box Friday — worth monitoring.
• Nasdaq weekly cloud 5 for 5 (consolidation/bullish breakout); Nasdaq 100 vs S&P 500 looks like a long-term bullish breakout, nothing like 1998–2000.
• Credit: BKLN near all-time highs, unconcerned.
• Action: took profits on another 10% of SMH (20% total) after it closed below the 10-week average — position sizing, not a trend call.
• Conclusion: constructive; short-term semis weakness managed via position size while the long-term trend stays intact.

summaries.title: Should The Bulls Be Confident Or Concerned?
summaries.reason: Every key indicator — defensive-staples ratios, breadth, credit, sector ratios, and moving-average structure — still reads risk-on with the secular bull market intact. The bulls should be confident; none of the 2022 or 2007/2018 warning patterns are present.
summaries.summary:
• Context: Middle East tensions, but crude trades mid-$70s, not back near $100.
• Defensives: staples (XLP) vs large-cap growth (SPYG) down 3.81% on the week, batting 0 for 5 on the weekly cloud; no 2007- or 2018/2022-style migration into defensives.
• Tech: XLK vs SPY retraced to 38.2%, trying to hold the rising daily cloud; no 2022 MA clustering/rollover; volatility confined near the 20/50-day averages.
• Breadth: NYSE A/D line making higher highs with no January 2022 divergence; AD volume line looks more like 1996–97 than 2000.
• Credit: BKLN leveraged loans show a bullish breakout and consolidation.
• Inflation watch: CRB broke its multi-year downtrend vs the S&P, but Dow-vs-Nasdaq ratio batting 0 for 5 — the opposite of Q1 2022.
• Nasdaq 100: above the 2000 peak and a rising 200-week average — a bullish breakout over long-term consolidation.
• Verdict: still risk-on, still a secular bull; near-term volatility is normal and should be ignored.

summaries.title: Four Questions For Investors On The 4th Of July
summaries.reason: All four questions resolved bullishly: the tape still leads with tech, shows no defensive or inflation-fear rotation, and no recession signal. The screens and fresh risk-on historical signals (high beta over high quality) point to continued upside, and they stayed long with only a token 10% semis trim.
summaries.summary:
• Method: five-round ETF screening — 389 ETFs reduced to 44 leaders; four questions answered.
• Q1 — shift away from tech/AI? No: 27 of 44 passing ETFs are tech-related, averaging 4.96/5 bullish checks, 98% above the monthly cloud.
• Q2 — market on the ropes? No: leadership is aggressive, not defensive — no bonds, staples, healthcare, utilities, or energy made the cut.
• Q3 — inflation/Fed/rates? No risk-off rotation: defensive staples (XLP) vs large-cap growth batting 0 for 5, the opposite of Q1 2022; energy (XLE) shows no inflation hedging either.
• Q4 — recession? No: short-term treasuries (SHY) vs SPYG printed an all-time low, not the 2008/COVID turtling pattern.
• Fresh Sentiment Trader signal (high beta vs high quality back above risk-on threshold): historically +12.84% avg S&P 500 return 12 months later, higher 87% of the time.
• Position: took profits on 10% of semis; left a second planned 10% sale unexecuted since uptrends since Aug 2025 remain intact.
• Conclusion: evidence reads risk-on; allocation matches it.

summaries.title: Semiconductors Flashed A Warning In 2000 - Are They Doing It Again?
summaries.reason: Semis show none of the 2000 warning signs yet (full-bore bullish weekly and daily clouds, SOX/S&P batting five-or-six-for-six), so the parabolic move is treated as a consolidation risk rather than a trend change; they trimmed 10% of SMH purely as prudent profit-taking.
summaries.summary:
• Question: are semis repeating the 2000 warning? In 2000, SOX topped months before the S&P and showed clear deterioration (price slicing the 10-week MA, MA rollover, first weekly close below the cloud on Sept 29, 2000).
• Present-day weekly cloud: still full-bore bullish — price above all MAs, slopes up, cloud rising. None of the 2000 warning signs present.
• SOX/S&P daily cloud batting five-or-six-for-six.
• Price remains above the 38.2/50/61.8% retracement levels — no 2000-style lower highs or undercutting.
• Risk management: trimmed 10% of SMH given the near-parabolic vertical move — a psychological trade, not a prediction.
• Rotation: RSP/XLK is a countertrend move within a downtrend, not a leadership change.
• Credit not screaming inflation; market action doesn't align with Fed hikes.
• Base case: secular bull lasting to 2034–35; 8–10% pullbacks are normal and expected.
• Conclusion: no evidence of trend change — constructive.

summaries.title: Is The New Fed Chair A Negative Gamechanger For Stocks?
summaries.reason: The weight of the evidence - very strong secular volatility model scores, monthly Bollinger Bands still in secular-bull form, and relative-strength charts far removed from January 2022 - indicates the new Fed chair's press conference is not yet a gamechanger; as long as earnings hold up, the secular bull is unlikely to end.
summaries.summary:
• Question: is the new Fed chair a negative gamechanger after his press conference spooked markets?
• How secular bulls end: never one event — inflation, rates, valuations, recession risk, and confidence must all cross a tipping point (as in 1968 and 2000).
• Volatility model: secular volatility scores are very strong — among the strongest periods of a secular bull.
• Monthly Bollinger Bands: S&P still well above with a secular-bull look, unlike the 1968 and 2000 peaks.
• Key line: "as long as earnings hold up, it's very difficult to envision the secular bull ending."
• Charts that flagged 2022 look nothing like today: Nasdaq/S&P and AIQ/tech relative strength at multi-month highs; AVWAP lines above price and turning up; XLE/XLK and WTI/S&P far from 2022 highs.
• Sentiment: fifth straight week with more bears than bulls, near all-time highs — contrarian support.
• Caveat: new chair dislikes forward guidance; data suggest aggressive 2022-style hikes are unlikely.
• Conclusion: not a gamechanger yet; concerns rise only if charts morph into 2022-like looks.

summaries.title: Tech & SpaceX: Will Inflation Cause Major Losses?
summaries.reason: Charts show a full-bore bullish look on tech (XLK, XLK/SPY, and the quarterly tech/S&P ratio) while credit markets treat inflation as an issue but not a showstopper; the setup resembles 2021/2016 far more than January 2022, so major inflation-driven losses are not currently indicated.
summaries.summary:
• Framework: inflation can be "a relevant topic" without being "a showstopper" — the question is what the charts say.
• Credit markets: WTI/IEF/LQD/Dow bond index show bullish breakouts and healthy consolidations above rising VWAP lines — not 2022-style bearish breakdowns.
• No crisis signal: IEF/LQD ratio shows no 2008- or COVID-style spike.
• Tech: Dow/Nasdaq weekly cloud full-bore bullish; tech vs S&P (FSPTX/VFINX) batting six-for-six on the quarterly cloud, breaking out like 2016 — argues against rotating to equal-weight RSP.
• XLK and XLK/SPY: full-bore bullish daily looks above rising MAs, support at 38.2%/50% retracements.
• Breadth: NYSE A/D and volume lines resemble the 1990s uptrend, not 2000/2008/2022 peaks.
• SpaceX IPO (June 12, +19% debut) doesn't change the setup.
• Conclusion: present day looks significantly better than January 2022; stay patient, reassess only if charts morph into 2022-like looks.

summaries.title: Did The Tech Bubble Just Pop?
summaries.reason: Nearly every chart and signal is green — a fresh breakout from a 6-year base, full-bore bullish MA clusters, hated (not euphoric) sentiment, valuation at its 5-year average, and multiple historical signals with strongly positive forward returns. The sharp Friday sell-off is treated as a normal giveback, so the stance is confidently bullish.
summaries.summary:
• AIQ vs RSP: bullish breakout from a 6-year base, retest, and higher high, MAs converging and turning up — favorable if it holds.
• No deflationary-bear signs: IEF vs SPY just made a new low; inflation is 'a concern but not a show stopper,' with the ratio rejected at prior resistance lines.
• AIQ vs XLP shows a bullish MA convergence and a higher high — the opposite of the bearish look that preceded the January 2022 peak.
• The QQQ/SPY slope since 2020 looks nothing like the 1998-2000 blow-off; NDX at 24.7x forward earnings is at its 5-year average — 'not 1999, not 2021.'
• A signal fired June 5: in all 11 historical cases the S&P was higher a year later (avg +16.9%) with muted drawdowns; May rallies >5% were followed by gains every time since 1950.
• Sentiment is skeptical, not euphoric: AAII shows the bull run is 'hated'; tech-leadership signals fired twice — QQQ higher 6-9 months later in every case (avg 12-month gain 38.3%).
• XLK vs SPY is a textbook full-bore bullish look with a tight MA cluster; the Nasdaq weekly cloud bats 5/5 with thick green support below price.
• Versus the dot-com bubble: 1991-2000 ran 9 years extended with no base; today shows ~3 years and a fresh breakout, with Friday's sharp sell-off and the Dow/Nasdaq cloud (0/5) as concerns.
• Conclusion: this does not look like a bubble — breakout, valuation, sentiment, and momentum all favor patience and better outcomes.

summaries.title: Tech Rally:  Too Far Or Early Stages?
summaries.reason: The charts read confidently as the early stages of a bullish trend — a full-bore bullish moving-average look, a 5-for-5 quarterly cloud, and a long-term breakout from consolidation dating to the 2000 peak — though the host keeps the door open to morphing into 2022/2000-style bearish looks if the evidence shifts.
summaries.summary:
Tech rally question framed via FSPTX/VFINX (tech vs. S&P 500) compared with the 1998-2000 blow-off and later bearish morphs; the present-day read is bullish.
• Present-day chart: the 20-day MA (blue) is on top, the 250-day (black) on the bottom, price above all MAs, tight clustering with slopes turning up — 'not a clean full-bore bullish look, but by definition, it is.'
• It doesn't look like January 2022 (fastest MA at the bottom), Q4 2018, H2 2011, or September 2000 when the bear market accelerated.
• 2000 reference: the Nasdaq lost 77.92% peak-to-trough and the S&P over 50% — but deterioration took time and showed a discernibly different chart look.
• The monthly cloud for tech/S&P is 'the polar opposite' of the bubble-burst look and similar to the bullish 2016 turn; the weekly cloud resembles a bottoming/bullish turn like Q1 2023.
• The quarterly cloud is batting 5-for-5 bullish for tech vs. S&P, including a long-term breakout from consolidation dating back to the 2000 peak.
• Blind test: shown without context, the chart would clearly be classified as 'the early stages of a bullish trend,' not a bearish one.
• The long-term breakout aligns with the secular-bull base case driven by demographics and an AI productivity tailwind; tech leadership matters because tech is such a large S&P weight.
• Caveats: breakout attempts can fail and retests of resistance are normal; concerns would increase if charts morph into 2000/2022-style looks — remain open-minded.

summaries.title: Which Leadership Narratives Are Backed By The Charts?
summaries.reason: Leadership evidence is broadly green — defensives at 0-for-5 all-time lows, a wide list of 5-for-5 leaders, and a market not getting defensive — but Ciovacco repeatedly stresses 'not confident' 5-for-5s and incremental (not overweight) exposure, so the stance is constructive-with-caution.
summaries.summary:
• The 2026 narratives — Fed cuts broadening the rally into equal-weight RSP and financials XLF — fail the test: both are batting 0 for 5 on the monthly cloud.
• 5-for-5 leaders vs. the S&P 500: AI/tech (AIQ), data centers (DTCR), global tech, triple Qs, equal-weight tech (RSPT), VGT, SPYG, Japan (DXJ), European financials (EUFN), Spain, Taiwan (EMXC), South Korea (EWY), gold (GLD), uranium (URA), metals/mining (XME), and telecom (XTL).
• Foreign stocks (ACWX vs. IWF/VOO) show observable improvement — first time above multi-year trend lines since 2011 — but many 5-for-5s are 'not confident', so exposure stays incremental, not an overweight.
• Defensives tell the real story: AGG, BIL, IEF, and XLP are all 0 for 5 at new all-time lows — the market is NOT getting defensive, unlike late 2021 into 2022 or the 2008 fear spike.
• Small caps (RSP/SPSM), financials, materials (XLB), and energy (XLE) remain long-term losers vs. the S&P; no 1970s energy repeat signal.
• SPY in isolation is 5 for 5; 2026 looks more like the 2025 pullback that made a stand at the blue span than Q1 2022's lower-low failure.
• XLK vs. ACWX: the advantage goes to tech — everything happens above a green cloud — so if forced to overweight one, it's an easy call.
• Conclusion: the secular bull thesis (demographics, productivity, through 2035) is confirmed; the chart evidence 'unequivocally shows material improvement' while keeping an open mind.

summaries.title: War: Have Stocks Started To Form A Sustainable Low?
summaries.reason: Ciovacco explicitly calls the tape 'a decent start, but still indecisive' and 'too early to answer' whether a sustainable low is in. Constructive elements (indexes holding key levels, credit firm, growth ratios batting 5/5) are balanced by real downside risks (oil and commodity ratios, a chart at a new closing high), making NEUTRAL the honest classification.
summaries.summary:
• Markets historically bottom early in wars; the S&P rose 3.36% and the Nasdaq +4.44% for the week amid the Iran/Strait conflict.
• Nearly every economically relevant country except Iran wants the strait reopened; markets find footing when news becomes 'less bad,' as at the April 2025 tariff low.
• The futures low near 6350 is the bull/bear guidepost: while it holds, patience is easy; if taken out, focus shifts to defensive priorities.
• The nine-week streak of down Thursdays ended; the only prior case (Oct 1998) was followed by a 59% S&P gain into March 2000.
• Oil futures calmed from ~$78 to ~$73 but remain an issue; even in a best case, the market could stay volatile in a narrow range near the lows.
• All four major indexes held at their anchored-VWAP lines and retracement levels and rallied back above them — 'so far, so good,' but a lot of work remains; a decent start, still indecisive.
• Credit markets (JNK, LQD) are holding support near logical regions and look far better than January 2022; MGK/RSP and semis vs SPX still look like uptrends.
• Growth ratios (SPYG vs SPY, vs SPYV) still bat 5/5 on monthly clouds and April 2026 still looks like a secular bull market — but XLF/XLK and RSP/XLK bat 0/5.
• One chart made a new closing high suggesting possible further downside; it's explicitly too early to say whether the low is in, so keep a wide open mind.

summaries.title: Will Stagflation Kill The Secular Bull Market In Stocks?
summaries.reason: The most balanced of the five: Hormuz uncertainty, the oil/stocks ratio, XLE/ARKF vulnerability and 'mitigation one' defensive planning raise near-term caution, but every longer-term chart (tech, breadth, bonds) still reads as a countertrend pullback within a secular bull that should be followed by a higher high.
summaries.summary:
Strait of Hormuz is 'ground zero' for the bull-bear debate; near-term uncertainty is high, so the video assembles bull/bear reference points.
• The S&P 500 sits near its upward-sloping 200-day MA (~6,600); above it patience is easier, while a sustained break below would raise bearish probabilities.
• Oil vs. stocks: the crude/SPY ratio remains below a downward-sloping AVWAP cluster despite the spike, and monthly PPO is nowhere near the zero line — a countertrend oil move within a longer trend favoring stocks.
• Crude under $115/barrel keeps the bull case comfortable; sustained trading above $115 would raise concern.
• Tech vs. S&P (FTEC/SPY) made a new all-time high off a turned-up 50-month MA; FTEC/SPYG is 4-for-5 bullish on the monthly cloud; QQQ/VTV weakness looks countertrend above a rising 200-week MA with the Coppock turning up.
• RSP/XLK is 0-for-5 on the monthly cloud — no trend flip toward equal-weight; SPYG/RSP is 6-for-6, still favoring large-cap growth.
• The bond market shows nothing like January 2022 (IEF weekly cloud, short-term bonds) — no inflation-panic signal.
• Breadth and monthly clouds (Nasdaq 100, NYSE A/D) still resemble normal-pullback secular bull scenarios, not the 2000 or 2008 setups.
• Risks to respect: XLE/SPY looks different from the past (potentially a painful cyclical drawdown) and ARKF's trend is more vulnerable — the firm is approaching 'mitigation one' (defensive action within the secular bull).
• Conclusion: evidence points to a pullback within an existing uptrend — a 10-15% drawdown followed by a higher high is the base case, not a stagflation-driven bear market.

summaries.title: The Case For A Magnificent Seven Rally
summaries.reason: The case for a Mag 7 rally is constructive — the 50% retracement holding on a thickening green cloud, a bullish DeMark target near +20%, the tariff catalyst from the Supreme Court ruling, and tame credit markets — but Ciovacco explicitly calls it tentative ('thinner ice', lower-probability turn), stopping short of very bullish.
summaries.summary:
• MAGS retraced 50% of the April 2025 rally and is bouncing; price is retracing above a thickening, upward-sloping green cloud — potential strong support.
• DeMark tools flagged the exhaustion beforehand; the upside propulsion target sits at 75.45, roughly +20% from 62.54, pairing with the retracement work.
• The Supreme Court striking down President Trump's tariffs could spark a rally; the S&P responded +47 points on Friday.
• IWY has retraced to former-resistance-now-support above a rising 200-week MA; a short stay below a rising MA is historically bullish, as after the 2022 lows.
• The Nasdaq 100/large-cap growth ratio made a stand at the 30-month MA, historically good for the S&P and tech — but the MA slope is more vulnerable than in past episodes.
• Monthly cloud: blue is back above red and the cloud flipped green, yet it's flattening and thin — 'skating on thinner ice', a lower-probability (not zero) turn back up.
• Credit markets look tame vs. the January 2022 warning; the S&P rally off the April 2025 low stays intact, with an 8% pullback zone counting as 100% normal.
• Foreign, cyclicals, and metals keep proving out on the long-term stack rank; they'd add incrementally if hurdles clear, but in a bull market 'when in doubt, leave it alone'.

summaries.title: Ten Pressing Questions For Investors
summaries.reason: The bull-market answer is a 'definitive yes' with broadening participation and intact tech/large-cap trends, but the tone is deliberately hedged — incremental moves only, gold/silver and foreign stocks near resistance, 'bulls make money, bears make money, but pigs get slaughtered.' Constructive but cautious.
summaries.summary:
• First question answered with a definitive yes — we are still clearly in a bull market; the most common human error is overtrading, and active traders consistently underperform.
• Participation is broadening: EM, ACWX, FNDF, and metals/mining (XME) ratios have been outperforming SPY since Q4 2024, with XME above a now upward-sloping 50-month MA.
• But aggressive allocation shifts are not prudent — XME and gold sit near anchored-VWAP resistance, and silver was down almost 32% in a single session; small incremental moves are preferred.
• Foreign stocks show observable improvement (FNDF ratio now on its 200-day MA) but still must clear 2021/2023 resistance; prior outperformance episodes were all given back, so stakes stay small.
• Tech and large-cap growth are not on the ropes: SPY, XLK, and VUG relative trends all hold well above anchored-VWAP support, and the rally off the April 2025 low remains intact.
• Leadership is strong in semis, gold miners, defense, foreign stocks, and large-cap growth — all owned; the S&P vs foreign stocks quarterly cloud bats 5/5.
• Gold vs SPY quarterly cloud is massively red, signaling resistance ahead; Fed-independence rhetoric is most likely overblown and the next Fed chair will likely stay independent.
• SPY, XLK, and SPYG still look good in isolation and relative terms, so the hurdles to make changes are high; tax costs of reallocating argue for sitting tight.
• Conclusion: stay close to buy-and-hold, avoid overtrading, and make only small incremental moves as new leadership trends confirm.

summaries.title: Is It Time To Underweight Tech Stocks?
summaries.reason: No compelling trend evidence to underweight tech: semis, QQQ/SPY and VGT sit at all-time highs with large-cap growth leadership intact, while rotation candidates (XLF/XLI/RSP) remain in downtrends — the conclusion is 'stay with the bull,' tempered by acknowledgement that several leadership trends could be in jeopardy.
summaries.summary:
Allocation review across 388 ETFs: the answer to underweighting tech is no — no compelling trend evidence to rotate out of XLK.
• Large-cap growth vs. S&P (Russell Top 200 Growth/SPY) still trends lower-left to upper-right, making a new all-time high in late 2025 above breakout levels and rising AWAP lines.
• Semis (SMH/SPY) hover at an all-time high — 'very difficult to think of tech being in trouble' with semis this healthy; the ITA/semis downtrend argues against dumping SMH for ITA.
• QQQ/SPY and VGT/SPY made new all-time highs after ~5 years of basing; recent tech underperformance is mild, with support below, and not alarming.
• No trend case for overweighting XLF/XLI: KBWB/SPY, XLI/XLK and RSP/XLK sit in downtrends or near all-time lows; XLF/XLK would first need to clear a downtrend line dating to 2020.
• Fed cut odds collapsed from ~11% to ~3-5% after Friday's NFP — weakening the broadening-out case for small caps and financials; tech performed well intraday.
• Rotation candidates are only 'small additions': EUFN made a new high but is a lower high vs. SPYG; ITA defense looks constructive; gold/miners (GDX/GLD/SLV/XME) show subtle bullish shifts but remain below key levels.
• Broad foreign stocks (ACWX/SPY) stay in a downtrend with a new all-time low — no broad international leadership yet.
• Conclusion: 'if you can't convince yourself to make a change, do nothing, trade less, and stay with the bull' — the bull market isn't on the ropes, though several leadership trends are potentially in jeopardy.

summaries.title: Is It Time To Dump The Magnificent Seven?
summaries.reason: Charts and flow signals argue against dumping the Mag 7 — the MGK/RSP ratio just broke out of a W base to a new all-time high, rotation-to-493 narratives are contradicted by the charts, and historical signals show the market higher a year later in nearly every case — while acknowledging a rollover remains possible.
summaries.summary:
• Model scores after the Nov 17 down day showed no vulnerability to a major reversal; long-term trend strength still 100 — no damage to the secular bull.
• MGK/RSP (Mag 7-heavy vs. equal weight) just broke out of a W base and printed a new all-time high in Q4 2025 — the opposite of the 2021 double-top that broke down bearishly in Q1 2022.
• The ratio sits well above rising weekly moving averages with a strong-trend look; the 2020-2021 yellow/orange Trend Meter flags that preceded the 2022 peak are absent today.
• RSP vs. MGK hasn't checked a single bullish cloud box — the 'dump the Mag 7, buy the 493' narrative is contradicted by the chart in front of them.
• Rotation talk to banks/financials isn't backed either: XLF/XLK and RSP/XLK just made new all-time lows; equal weight and financials remain in long-term downtrends vs. tech.
• Sentiment and flow signals are bullish: after similar setups XLK was higher a year later in most cases, hedge-fund-exposure signals were higher 100% of the time, and the high-beta signal showed a median +14.45%.
• In a secular bull they'd rather do nothing and ride the long-term leaders than anticipate a rollover; a sustained break below 6650-6800 would change the calculus.
• The AI story is a multi-year buildout (data centers are just the first layer, like electricity), supporting continued tech leadership.

summaries.title: What Could This Week's Sharp Reversal Mean For Stocks?
summaries.reason: The weight of the evidence remains constructive — long-term trend intact, breadth near another thrust, contrarian sentiment extremes (3x-short ETF bets, 3-year-low Bitcoin sentiment), and strong historical forward returns — but Ciovacco repeatedly hedges: 'not predicting anything,' a possible gap-fill head fake, and earlier yellow flags.
